statements.t: In June 2026, we expanded U.S. compatibility to include Abbott’s FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus sensor (“Libre 3 Plus”) and announced the U.S. rollout of Omnipod 5 algorithm enhancements, including a lower target glucose setting of 100 mg/dL.

In addition, we continue to advance the development of our fully closed-loop AID system for people with type 2 diabetes, including completion of enrollment in the EVOLVE pivotal study, which is intended to support a planned 510(k) submission in 2027.
Our Pod is intended to be used continuously for up to three days, after which it may be replaced with a new disposable Pod.
As we grow our customer base, we expect to generate an increasing portion of our revenues through sales of our disposable Pods, which provide a recurring revenue stream.
We estimate total costs associated with the MDCs will be approximately $50 million, most of which we expect to incur in 2026.

We do not expect tariffs to have a significant impact on our gross margin in 2026; however, the elimination of the current exemption for certain medical devices would have a material impact on our gross margin and results of operations in future periods.

The increases in research and development expenses for both periods were primarily due to continued investment in our Omnipod and pipeline products, including Omnipod 6, our next-generation AID system, and a fully closed-loop AID system for type 2 diabetes, partially offset by a reduction in incentive compensation expense due to lower expected achievement of company performance targets in the current year.

The increases for both periods were primarily attributable to higher personnel-related costs driven by increased headcount across our commercial, customer experience, regulatory, quality and other support functions, partially offset by a reduction in incentive compensation expense due to lower expected achievement of company performance targets in the current year.
We expect net interest expense for the full year 2026 to increase to approximately $40 million, primarily due to lower interest income.
We expect capital expenditures for 2026 to increase compared with 2025 to support our continued global manufacturing expansion plans.
We expect to fund our capital expenditures using existing cash and financing.

Investments in Developed Software —Investments in developed software were $13.1 million and $13.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and were primarily related to projects supporting our cloud-based capabilities.
We expect to allocate approximately $400 million toward repurchases in 2026, funded with existing cash.
In addition, there may be other risks and uncertainties that we are unable to predict at this time or that we currently do not expect to have a material adverse effect on our business.
